title: Sky v1 system checks 9 and 10 (incl. Amendment 1 H and I)

items.question: System check 9: follow-ups in grokking-v1 - no label takes more than 50 % of them while other labels still have candidates (Amendment 1 H: may fail by design; reported literally over the request order as a declared deviation).
items.definition_used: Order: ri_runs.ri_run_id of the grokking-v1 follow-up curves (the order in which follow-ups were recorded = completion order, a proxy for followups.rowid, which DR1 lacks; ri_run_id order equals created_at order). Label: latest label (no label was assigned after its follow-up was recorded; the label named in 467 reasons agrees with it in every case, boundary reasons name none). Stream: the curve's meta followup_reason. Candidates of a label at follow-up i: grokking-v1 objects of that label with finished_at <= created_at of follow-up i and not followed up at or before i. Violation at i: the largest cumulative label share over follow-ups 1..i is > 50 % and some other label has >= 1 candidate. Evaluated over every prefix (literal, i = 1 included). Sensitivity readings: S1 the cumulative share at the end of each scheduler call (the follow-ups form 10 disjoint blocks of 70 (last 59), one per 600 s call, so these points are exact in request order); candidates at the estimated call time (daemon's period: t_daemon + 600 s x k, with t_daemon the smallest offset at which every call's picks had finished), and at a lower bound (the latest finish among the call's picks). S2 the request order reconstructed inside each call from the scheduler's stream round robin. S3 the per-call share. S4 the final share.
items.literal_result: 25 of 689 prefixes violate; first violation at i = 1 (smooth, trivial single pick); 3 spells: follow-ups 1-1 (1 follow-up(s), 0 s), majority smooth, max share 100.0 % at i = 1 (smooth, +50.0 pp, surplus 1 follow-ups); follow-ups 3-3 (1 follow-up(s), 0 s), majority memorization, max share 66.7 % at i = 3 (memorization, +16.7 pp, surplus 1 follow-ups); follow-ups 5-27 (23 follow-up(s), 102 s), majority memorization, max share 66.7 % at i = 6 (memorization, +16.7 pp, surplus 4 follow-ups). Last violation at i = 27 (first call). Excluding i = 1: 24 violating prefixes. S2 reconstructed request order: 36 violating prefixes, all at i <= 41. S1 call ends: violations after calls none. Final shares: smooth 47.9 %, memorization 34.3 %, grokking 17.9 %
items.amended_result: Amendment 1 H keeps the criterion and asks for a literal report over the request order, with the expected failure declared as a deviation. Over the reconstructed request order the check fails (36 prefixes, all in the first call). At exact call boundaries it holds (max 47.9 %). Per call: call 7: smooth 37 of 70 (52.9 %), candidates left of other labels {'grokking': 9, 'memorization': 69}; call 8: smooth 40 of 70 (57.1 %), candidates left of other labels {'grokking': 0, 'memorization': 48}; call 9: smooth 36 of 70 (51.4 %), candidates left of other labels {'grokking': 0, 'memorization': 14}. The label-blind matched and boundary streams made 387 of 689 picks (56.2 %, about 2/3 in calls 2-7). No anomaly-stream follow-ups.

items.interpretation: Read literally, check 9 fails, but only at the very start. In completion order 25 of 689 prefixes violate, all within the first scheduler call (i <= 27 of its 70 picks). Prefix 1 is trivial (a single pick is 100 %). Without it, the majority label (memorization) never exceeds 66.7 % and is never more than 4 picks ahead of the other labels combined, while other labels had candidates. In the reconstructed request order the picture is the same (36 prefixes, all at i <= 41; max 75.0 % at i = 4). At every call boundary, where the cumulative counts are exact in request order, no label exceeds 50 %. The largest end-of-call share is 47.9 % (smooth, after the last call, when nothing is left). The failure Amendment 1 H anticipated, one label dominating the region, does not occur: smooth is 47.9 % of the region. The by-design mechanism is still visible per call: in calls [7, 8, 9] smooth took 52.9 %, 57.1 %, 51.4 % of the picks while memorization (and in the first of them grokking) still had candidates. That happened as the grokking candidates ran out and the label-blind boundary/matched picks followed the smooth-heavy remainder.
items.caveats: DR1 has no followups table, so request order is unknown and completion order is a proxy. Within a call, requests are claimed by priority (matched/boundary 2.0 before stratified/random_control 1.5), so stratified picks complete last in each block. Completion order is therefore biased against label balance inside a call. The S2 reconstruction assumes that order within a stream equals completion order. Call-end points do not depend on either. Call times are estimated, but every estimate falls inside its bracket and after all of that call's picks had finished. Prefix i = 1 is a trivial violation. Labels: every latest label was recorded within 0.04 s of the object's finish, before its follow-up, and agrees with the label named in the follow-up reason; earlier labels are not in DR1.

items.question: System check 10: anomalies flagged at about 1 % per (region, label) group, each looked at by hand (Amendment 1 I: evaluated offline on the final catalog for every v1 group; per-group result literal, overall rate as a declared deviation).
items.definition_used: Offline: tycho.analysis.anomaly.anomaly_scores per (region, label) group of the DR1 objects (all 1223 are done, labelled and not diverged, as the scheduler requires). Summary mapping = the object's objects.parquet row, which holds every key summary_features reads (t_train_acc90, t_test_acc90, steps_total, final_train_acc, final_test_acc, final_train_loss, final_test_loss, plateau_logfrac, n_drops, test_bump). Flagged iff score >= THRESHOLD = 8.0. Groups with fewer than MIN_GROUP = 20 objects are not scored. 'About 1 %' is ambiguous; chosen reading: the group's flag count is consistent with a 1 % rate (exact two-sided binomial test vs p = 0.01, p >= 0.05). Alternatives: (a) not too many (one-sided P(X >= k) >= 0.05); (b) a fixed band 0.5 % <= k/n <= 2 %. Literal (as run) reading: the flags the survey itself acted on, i.e. scheduler follow-ups whose reason starts with 'anomaly'. The scheduler scores grokking-v1 only.

items.interpretation: Overall, the offline flag rate is about the intended 1 % (13 of 1212 = 1.07 %). The per-group criterion still fails, in one group: markov-v1/smooth. There, the 12 flags are all 12 seeds of a single configuration (1:1.0;1,2,3:1.0 chain). Its runs are ordinary smooth fits, but they are the only Markov runs whose train accuracy reaches the rescaled 90 % threshold (reached in 1 of 24 coupling x context cells). The flag is therefore a grouping artefact: the (region, label) group pools 24 task regimes, and the censored-time feature has MAD 0. These are not curves that defy their label. The remaining flag (parity-k4/smooth) is a borderline early loss spike in a successful run. The grokking-v1 groups have 0 flags (largest scores grokking 3.12, memorization 7.12, smooth 7.82). That matches the 0 anomaly follow-ups, and so does the reconstructed scheduler view at each call. The 'unknown' exit thus gave no grokking follow-up in v1, and the 13 offline flags lie in in-situ regions the scheduler never scores.
items.caveats: The pre-registration does not define 'about 1 %'. With 33 to 330 scored objects per group, a 1 % rate means 0.3 to 3.3 expected flags, so 0 is the typical outcome for small groups. Under the 0.5-2 % band every scored group fails; under the binomial reading small groups can pass. Flags cluster by configuration (2 configurations hold all 13), so the effective sample for the overall rate is the number of configurations (hence the wide bootstrap interval). Features come from objects.parquet, not the catalog's summary_json; the keys are the same. parity-k2/double_descent (11 objects) is below MIN_GROUP and never scored. The scheduler's call times are estimated.
